# everpure_azure_volume_group (Resource)

Manages a Volume Group — a set of volumes sharing performance limits and a snapshot protection schedule, on a Storage Pool.

~> **Destroying a volume group soft-deletes it and everything inside it.** The backend disconnects any hosts and destroys the volume group's volumes along with it as one unit; all of it stays recoverable until eradication. Volumes Terraform destroyed before the group are soft-deleted separately and must each be recovered on their own. See [Deletion policies](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/guides/deletion-policies).

To read a volume group managed elsewhere without taking ownership of it, use the [`everpure_azure_volume_group` data source](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/data-sources/azure_volume_group).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "storage_pool_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Full ARM ID of an existing Everpure Storage Pool in the same subscription."
}

resource "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  name            = "vg-prod-east"
  storage_pool_id = var.storage_pool_id

  # Both omitted below means unlimited. Removing either attribute from
  # configuration clears an existing limit; both can be changed in place.
  bandwidth_limit_in_mbps = 500
  iops_limit              = 5000

  # Absent means no snapshot schedule. Can be added, changed or removed in
  # place; removing it disables the schedule.
  snapshot_protection_policy {
    frequency = "PT1H"
    retention = "P7D"
  }

  tags = {
    environment = "prod"
  }
}

# A volume group cloned from an existing one. Every source_* attribute is
# create-only: changing source_type or any source_*_id forces a new volume
# group to be created.
resource "everpure_azure_volume_group" "clone" {
  name                   = "vg-prod-east-clone"
  storage_pool_id        = var.storage_pool_id
  source_type            = "volumeGroup"
  source_volume_group_id = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id

  # Overrides the defaults, which normally protect a volume group from destroy.
  deletion_protection  = false # true (default) blocks destroy + replace
  eradicate_on_destroy = true  # false (default) soft-deletes, recoverable
}

output "volume_group_id" {
  value = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
}

output "volume_group_internal_id" {
  value = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.internal_id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the volume group. The name must be 2-40 characters, start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, numbers and hyphens. Changing this forces a new volume group to be created.
- `storage_pool_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the Storage Pool this volume group lives on. Changing this forces a new volume group to be created.

### Optional

- `bandwidth_limit_in_mbps` (Number) Bandwidth limit for the volume group, in megabytes per second (MB/s). Omit for no limit. Removing this attribute from configuration clears an existing limit. Can be changed in place.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether to block destroying this volume group, or replacing it (which destroys it as part of the replacement). Defaults to `true`. Set to `false`, and apply, before a destroy or a change that would otherwise force replacement.
- `eradicate_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether destroy permanently eradicates the volume group (and the volumes inside it) instead of soft-deleting it. Defaults to `false`. There is no recovery window once eradicated.
- `iops_limit` (Number) I/O operations per second (IOPS) limit for the volume group. Omit for no limit. Must be at least 100. Removing this attribute from configuration clears an existing limit. Can be changed in place.
- `snapshot_protection_policy` (Block List) The volume group's snapshot schedule. Absent means no schedule. Can be added, changed or removed in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--snapshot_protection_policy))
- `source_recoverable_volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the soft-deleted volume group to recover. Required when `source_type` is `recoverableVolumeGroup`, and must be unset otherwise. Changing this forces a new volume group to be created.
- `source_snapshot_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group snapshot to restore from. Required when `source_type` is `snapshot`, and must be unset otherwise. Terraform needs read access to the snapshot's volume group, not just the snapshot. Changing this forces a new volume group to be created.
- `source_type` (String) How the volume group's initial contents are created. One of `none` (empty, the default), `volumeGroup` (clone from `source_volume_group_id`), `snapshot` (restore from `source_snapshot_id`), or `recoverableVolumeGroup` (recover from `source_recoverable_volume_group_id`). Changing this forces a new volume group to be created.
- `source_volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group to clone from. Required when `source_type` is `volumeGroup`, and must be unset otherwise. Changing this forces a new volume group to be created.
- `tags` (Map of String) A mapping of tags to assign to the volume group. Can be changed in place. Some environments append their own tags outside Terraform (e.g. an Azure Policy, or the resource provider itself); including those tags in this configuration, or excluding them via a `lifecycle.ignore_changes` block, avoids a persistent diff against them.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group, e.g. `/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool1/volumeGroups/vg1`.
- `internal_id` (String) Everpure's internal ID of the volume group.

<a id="nestedblock--snapshot_protection_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `snapshot_protection_policy`

Required:

- `frequency` (String) How often to take a snapshot, as an ISO 8601 duration using days or smaller units, e.g. `"PT1H"` or `"P1D"`.
- `retention` (String) How long to keep snapshots taken by this schedule, as an ISO 8601 duration using days or smaller units, e.g. `"P7D"`.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Defaults to 20 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when creating the volume group.
- `delete` (String) Defaults to 35 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when destroying the volume group, including eradicating its recoverable copy when eradicate_on_destroy is set.
- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the volume group.
- `update` (String) Defaults to 20 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when updating the volume group.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = everpure_azure_volume_group.example
  identity = {
    subscription_id     = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
    storage_pool_name   = "pool-prod-east"
    name                = "vg-prod-east"
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  # ... configuration matching the imported volume group
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the volume group.
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the resource lives in.
- `storage_pool_name` (String) Name of the storage pool the volume group belongs to.
- `subscription_id` (String) Azure subscription ID the resource lives in.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Volume groups are imported by their full Azure resource ID.
terraform import everpure_azure_volume_group.example \
  "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east/volumeGroups/vg-prod-east"
```
